comment: Differences between fireemu and the official Local Emulator Suite that are intended and written down. A key is <scenarioId>#<stepId>. `documents` must name the text that publishes the divergence (a README section, a capability manifest entry, or a specification section); `reason` says what the difference is. Everything not listed here that differs is recorded as debt in DEBT.md, and `pnpm run check` gates a listed row against its recorded fireemu value, so a documented divergence still cannot drift silently.

firestore/missing-composite-index#admin-.reason: Under firestore.indexValidationPolicy = firebase, a query whose composite index is not in the index file is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION and the fragment production would need. The official Firestore emulator serves the query as if the index existed; fireemu offers that as the `emulator` policy instead of as the default.
Same policy difference for an equality plus an inequality on another field.

firestore/missing-composite-index#client.reason: The same refusal reaches the gRPC client SDK: the target is removed with FAILED_PRECONDITION and the query resolves empty rather than failing the whole stream, so the client stays usable.

firestore/lite-rest-transport#query-need.reason: The same policy difference over the REST transport, where the SDK surfaces it as `failed-precondition`.

firestore/rest-error-shapes#runQuery-nee.reason: The REST envelope of the same refusal: HTTP 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION with the index fragment, where the official emulator answers 200 with results.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-a-re.reason: The official Local Emulator Suite serves no App Check exchange route at all, so the oracle answers 404. fireemu issues a locally signed token for a registered debug secret.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-an-u.reason: No route on the oracle (404) against the specified 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "App attestation failed." that fireemu returns for an unknown project, app, disabled app or secret alike.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-a-li.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-REPLAY-1 (crates/fireemu/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md sections 17 and 23
appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-a-li.reason: No route on the oracle (404). fireemu fails closed with 501 UNIMPLEMENTED / APP_CHECK_REPLAY_UNSUPPORTED rather than issuing a reusable token for a limited-use request.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#jwks.reason: The official suite serves no JWKS route (404). fireemu publishes this instance's single public App Check key as an RFC 7517 JWK Set.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#firest.reason: The oracle issues no App Check token, so it cannot run the valid-token column at all; the row records the same request without the field and marks itself `noTokenIssuedBySide`.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#auth-s.reason: The oracle issues no App Check token; see the Firestore row.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#storag.reason: The oracle issues no App Check token; see the Firestore row.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#callab.reason: The oracle issues no token, so its callable sees no app. fireemu forwards the verified token and the callable receives request.app with the registered app id, which is what section 13.4 requires of an unenforcing callable.

The official Functions emulator runs the runtime with token verification skipped, so any value in the field becomes an app with a null id. fireemu removes an unverifiable field before the runner can decode it, so the callable sees no app: strictly safer, and deliberately different.
Two App Check fields are ambiguous. The official emulator accepts the folded value as an app; fireemu classifies it as malformed and removes it.
The oracle issues no token, so its enforcing callable answers 401. fireemu presents a verified token and the callable runs with request.app populated.

With verification skipped, the official emulator admits an unverifiable token into an enforceAppCheck callable. fireemu refuses it with the callable 401 UNAUTHENTICATED envelope before the handler runs.
Duplicate App Check fields are admitted by the official emulator and refused by fireemu, for the same reason as the unenforcing row.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#on-req.reason: The oracle issues no token, so it sends no field and its onRequest handler counts zero. Both sides pass the raw field list through unclassified, which is what the row is about.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-ENFORCE-1 (crates/fireemu/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md sections 12.1 and 17
appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.reason: The official emulators have no enforcement mode to configure, so they admit the request. This is the whole point of the variant: fireemu denies with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED before Security Rules and before any side effect.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-ENFORCE-1 (crates/fireemu/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md sections 12.1 and 17
appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.reason: Same: no enforcement on the oracle; 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on fireemu.
Same: no enforcement on the oracle; fireemu treats duplicate fields as malformed and denies.
Both sides admit, but the oracle admits because it never looked and cannot present a token; the row is marked `noTokenIssuedBySide` so the agreement is not read as parity.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#auth-sig.reason: No enforcement on the oracle; fireemu denies the end-user Identity Toolkit route with 403 and consumes no credential.
Same as the missing-field row, for an ambiguous duplicate field.
Both admit; the oracle only because it never looked. Marked `noTokenIssuedBySide`.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#storage-.reason: No enforcement on the oracle; fireemu denies the Firebase Storage dialect with the 403 Storage JSON error envelope.
Same as the missing-field row, for an ambiguous duplicate field.
Both admit; the oracle only because it never looked. Marked `noTokenIssuedBySide`.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#callable.reason: The oracle issues no token, so its enforcing callable answers 401; fireemu presents a verified token and the handler runs with request.app.
The official Functions emulator skips token verification and admits an unverifiable token; fireemu refuses it with the callable 401 envelope before the handler runs.
Duplicate fields are admitted by the official emulator and refused by fireemu.

functions/callable-auth-context#a-forged.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-FUNCTIONS-1, "callable Authorization integrity" (crates/fireemu/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md section 25 decision 3
functions/callable-auth-context#a-forged.reason: The official Functions emulator runs the runtime with token verification skipped, so any Bearer value produces a context with hasAuth true and a null uid. fireemu verifies the ID token against the target project's registry and reinserts only a resolved user, so a forged value produces no Auth context at all.

functions/callable-auth-context#bearer-o.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-FUNCTIONS-1, "callable Authorization integrity" (crates/fireemu/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md section 25 decision 3
functions/callable-auth-context#bearer-o.reason: `Bearer owner` is the privileged emulator credential. The official emulator hands it to the callable as an authenticated context with a null uid; fireemu never treats it as a callable user identity.

functions/http-routing-cors-and-timeouts.reason: The official emulator starts its runtime with FIREBASE_DEBUG_FEATURES={"skipTokenVerification":true,"enableCors":true}, so firebase-functions wraps every handler in cors({origin: true}) and answers a preflight from any origin on the internet. fireemu serves the functions port to loopback origins only and answers 403 "forbidden origin" to the rest, the way its other ports do: a page a developer happens to have open must not be able to drive their local backend.

The same divergence on the request itself rather than the preflight: the official emulator reflects https://evil.example and hands the callable's result to it. fireemu refuses a non-loopback Origin with 403 before the request reaches the runner. An onRequest function on a loopback origin does get the CORS headers enableCors would have given it, so local browser development is unaffected.

storage-probe/fb-resumable-upload#upload.reason: fireemu checks X-Goog-Upload-Offset against the bytes already received and refuses a mismatch with 400, as production does. The official emulator never reads the offset: it appends whatever arrives, so a chunk sent with a wrong offset was measured to commit a corrupt object.

storage-probe/fb-resumable-upload#wrong-.reason: The consequence of the offset check: fireemu never published the mis-offset upload (404), the official emulator committed it.

storage-probe/rules-request-model#overwr.reason: An upload over an existing object evaluates the rules `update` method in fireemu, as production evaluates it. The official emulator evaluates every upload as `create` (its uploadObject hard-codes the CREATE method), so a rule that guards update was measured to admit an anonymous overwrite.

storage-probe/rules-request-model#cache-.reason: resource.cacheControl is a production rules field. fireemu passes it; the official emulator's rules resource omits it, so reading it raises and the read was measured to deny.

storage-probe/rules-request-model#conten.reason: The same for resource.contentLanguage: a production rules field the official emulator's rules resource omits.

storage-probe/gcs-resumable-upload#chunk.reason: fireemu serves the production Content-Range resumable protocol on the JSON API: an intermediate chunk is answered 308 Resume Incomplete with the persisted range. The official emulator ignores Content-Range entirely and finalizes on every PUT, so it was measured to commit the first 5-byte chunk as the whole object.
The second chunk of the same upload: fireemu completes the 10-byte object; the official emulator, having already finalized, answers 400.
The committed sizes the two protocols leave behind: 10 bytes under fireemu's chunk protocol, the truncated 5 under the official emulator.

storage-probe/gcs-preconditions#insert-i.reason: fireemu honours generation and metageneration preconditions as production honours them: ifGenerationMatch=0 on an existing object is 412. The official emulator parses no precondition parameter at all and was measured to overwrite.

storage-probe/gcs-preconditions#get-if-g.reason: A read whose ifGenerationNotMatch names the current generation is 304 Not Modified under fireemu, as in production; the official emulator ignores the parameter and serves the object.

storage-probe/gcs-preconditions#delete-i.reason: A delete guarded by a stale ifGenerationMatch is 412 under fireemu; the official emulator ignores the guard and was measured to delete the object.

storage-probe/gcs-preconditions#malforme.reason: A malformed precondition value is 400 under fireemu; the official emulator does not read the parameter (and, this late in the program, had already deleted the object the guarded delete should have kept).

storage-probe/gcs-preconditions#object-s.reason: The consequence of the guard: the object survives under fireemu and is gone under the official emulator.

storage-probe/gcs-checksums#mismatching-.reason: A declared md5Hash / X-Goog-Hash is verified against the received bytes before the commit, as production verifies it; a mismatch is 400 and nothing is published. The official emulator ignores declared checksums and was measured to store the corrupt payload.
The consequence: the refused upload does not exist under fireemu (404); the official emulator serves the object it should have refused.
The same verification for a crc32c declared in the metadata document of a multipart upload.

storage-probe/triggers#finalize-on-fireb.reason: fireemu's Storage events carry the production CloudEvent envelope (source names the bucket, subject names the object, the bucket extension attribute and datacontenttype are set) and the production selfLink / mediaLink hosts inside the object payload. The official emulator writes the object path into source, sets no subject, no bucket attribute and no datacontenttype, and links to its own emulator host. The object payload is otherwise identical field for field.

storage-probe/triggers#metadata-update-o.reason: The same envelope and link-host divergence on the metadataUpdated event.

storage-probe/triggers#finalize-on-overw.reason: The same envelope and link-host divergence on the finalize event of an overwrite.

storage-probe/triggers#finalize-on-json-.reason: The same envelope and link-host divergence on the finalize event a JSON API copy publishes for its destination.

storage-probe/triggers#delete.reason: The same envelope and link-host divergence on the delete event.

storage-probe/triggers#metadata-update-o.reason: The same envelope and link-host divergence on the metadataUpdated event that creating a download token publishes.

storage-probe/triggers#json-api-resumabl.reason: The same envelope and link-host divergence on the finalize event of a JSON API resumable upload.
